description.narrative: The identification of the Sootaga Mautu Faaleaoaoga’s priority area of reform is expected to inform the development of Samoa’s System Transformation Grant (STG) application. UNESCO has been selected as the Grant agent for the USD 2.5 million STG and will collaborate closely under the MEC’s leadership to prepare a high-quality program document for the STG application. Similar to the Compact’s development process, the STG development will involve participatory consultations with key stakeholders, including the Local Education Group (LEG), the Samoa Qualifications Authority (SQA), the National University of Samoa (NUS), the Education Sector Working Group (ESWG), other relevant ministries and other government agencies, civil society, parent teacher associations, community groups, and development partners. The program of Samoa’s System Transformation Grant targets the priority reform identified in the country’s Sootaga Mautu Faaleaoaoga, which is ensuring that multiple, relevant and inclusive seamless pathways are available to learners across all levels, underpinned by strong foundations. It aims to build a cohesive, inclusive education system in Samoa, where quality learning pathways are accessible to all learners, founded on quality early childhood education (ECE) through to vocational training and beyond. UNESCO, alongside the Ministry of Education and Culture (MEC) and other relevant stakeholders, will work to strengthen foundational learning, promote smooth transitions across educational stages, and ensure that education reflects cultural values and priorities.
